assertions.name: Sustainment EMERGES as eps -> 0 on the fixed 30-turnover horizon: eps>=1e-3 decays, eps=1e-4 sustains (Om_end/Om_max ~ 0.71)
assertions.source: DN q-shell, Kolmogorov load; transition near eps ~ 1e-3..1e-4. CONFOUND flagged: at eps=1e-4 the low-mode viscous time ~2/(eps*k1^2) ~ 2e4 turnovers >> horizon, so horizon-sustainment is consistent with slow viscous decay; the transient growth Om_max/Om0 ~ 3.9 does show active inertial transfer. Discriminator (next bean): horizon scaled to the viscous time / classical same-nu comparison. Scope (a).

description: SF1 (epic qou-a3n3): tests whether the QOU's finite low-mode core can act as its own forcing. Unforced Desnyansky-Novikov shell model with q-integer wavenumbers k_n=[n]_q and nu_q=(q-1)/(2q), N=12, Kolmogorov initial load, 30 eddy turnovers, RK2. Verdict per eps ladder: does enstrophy sustain (Om_end/Om_max > 0.5 or blow-up) or decay? Decay everywhere = the finite core cannot self-sustain its cascade — in-model evidence AGAINST the sustained-forcing blow-up channel at finite q; the channel would then require genuinely infinite-dimensional sustainment (the q->1 limit escaping every finite truncation). Scope (a); exploratory tier.
